frase_gancho.texto: A stone warrior who held up the roof of his temple.

puente_narrativo.texto: If this warrior held up the sky, another monument guarded the sacred earth. Continue to a wall that does not stop armies, but something harder: it separates the ordinary from the divine, with serpents that devour warriors.

guion_corto.texto: This stone warrior, more than four and a half meters tall, is no ordinary statue: it is a column. Together with three identical ones, it held up the roof of the temple that crowned Pyramid B at Tula. It is made of four blocks of basalt fitted together with tenons. It wears a tall feathered headdress, a butterfly-shaped pectoral, a spear-thrower in its right hand, and a bundle of darts in its left. If you could walk around it, you would see on its back a solar disk held by a belt of serpents. It is a deified warrior, standing, carrying the sky of its city. And its name was brought from Greece.

guion_largo.texto:
To understand this giant, we have to travel to Tula, in the present-day state of Hidalgo. After the fall of Teotihuacán, central Mexico went through centuries of upheaval, with cities such as Xochicalco, Cacaxtla and Teotenango, of which this hall also holds traces. Then, between the years 900 and 1150, more or less, Tula became the most powerful capital of its time. Its ancient name was Tollan, «the place of the reeds», the rushes that grow beside water.

The Atlantean figures were not decoration: they were columns. At the top of Pyramid B stood a temple, and its beamed roof rested on four figures like this one and on square pillars with warriors in relief. Each Atlantean figure is made of four blocks that fit one on top of another, like building pieces weighing several tons. Whoever entered the temple passed through a forest of stone warriors.

Whom do they represent? That is debated. They may be deified warriors of the military elite or the very god to whom the temple was dedicated, Tlahuizcalpantecuhtli, the Lord of the Morning Star, which is Venus seen at dawn. What we do see is the complete uniform: a tall feathered headdress, rectangular ear ornaments, a loincloth, sandals, and the butterfly on the chest, which is associated with the souls of warriors who died in combat.

If you could walk around it, you would discover its best-kept detail. On the back it wears a disk tied at the waist with a belt in the form of a fire serpent. The Toltec called it a [tezcacuitlapilli](mna_s05_disco_tezcacuitlapilli), the «mirror of the back», and it was an insignia of command. Further on you will see a piece of that kind, made with thousands of fragments of turquoise.

The name «Atlantean» is not Toltec. It comes from Atlas, the giant of Greek mythology who held up the sky on his shoulders. The Europeans who discovered these figures thought of him, and the name stuck. The Toltec never heard of Atlas, but they knew that a roof, and a sky, need someone to hold them up.

The city was explored in the late nineteenth century by the Frenchman Désiré Charnay, and from the 1940s onward by the Mexican archaeologist Jorge Acosta, who found the fragments of the Atlantean figures at the top of the pyramid. It is believed that they were toppled by those who destroyed the city around 1150. With the pieces, like a giant jigsaw puzzle, what you can see today was put together.

There is a detail that specialists still debate. At Chichén Itzá, in Yucatán, more than a thousand kilometers away, there is a temple with columns of warriors that are almost identical. Who influenced whom? Some think there were Toltec in Yucatán; others, that the exchange went in both directions. What is certain is that the two cities resemble each other so much that for decades it was hard to know where one ended and the other began. In the Maya Hall, a Chac Mool from Chichén will ask you the same question.

For the Mexica, who arrived in the valley centuries later, the Toltec were the artists and sages par excellence: it was said that they had invented all the arts, and the Mexica proclaimed themselves their heirs. When you look at this warrior, remember that it is not just a stone soldier watching you: it is the prestige of a people that others wanted to inherit.

texto.Origin: Tula, Hidalgo (Pyramid of Tlahuizcalpantecuhtli, Temple B)
texto.Dimensions: 4.83 m high x 1.00 m wide x 1.40 m deep
texto.Discovery: Recovered by Jorge R. Acosta in the late 1930s, in the trench of Pyramid B

texto.pregunta: Myth: The Toltec called these figures “Atlanteans.”
texto.respuesta: Reality: That name comes from Greek mythology and was given by Europeans; we do not know what the Toltec called them.
